edition.alertText: Trump says wants 'permanent' deal with Iran — tells reporters 'we're going to get it done'; Senate rejects binding war powers resolution 48-51 — Trump retains authority for continued operations; IRGC attacks Bahrain civilian oil facility in Sitra — first strike on civilian infrastructure; claims hits on US Patriot radars at al-Riffa and Awali air bases; UKMTO: 2 tanker attacks near Khasab on Nov 21 — engine-room fires, crews evacuated; tanker incident with military forces near Charbahar on Nov 22; Saudi intercepts 3 ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh (Nov 21); 5 drones + 3 BMs the previous day; 14+ Iranian tankers readying to break US naval blockade — Gharibabadi calls blockade 'act of war'; IRGC claims 58th MQ-9 Reaper downed; also claims 19th and 20th MQ-1 Predator drones shot down; Qatari delegation holds 2-hour talks in Tehran (Nov 20 evening) — 'progress on framework' per Qatar FM; Houthis building tunnels and fortifications at Bab al-Mandeb — tightening grip on second chokepoint; UKMTO: 263 ships transited Hormuz Nov 12-18, down 15% WoW — oil tankers fall from 52 to 37 (-29%); gold crashes to $3,532 — 5th straight daily fall, -10% weekly, lowest since March 2025; S&P 500 posts worst weekly loss (-8.6%) since Iran war began; copper -9.3% weekly; Brent rebounds to ~$92.57 on Monday morning futures; US gas falls to $3.69/gal — lowest since war began; Brent down nearly one-fifth in November

situation: The diplomatic landscape shifted over the weekend as Trump told reporters he wants a 'permanent' deal with Iran, saying 'we're going to get it done — not a little deal, a permanent deal,' while simultaneously the US Senate narrowly rejected a binding war powers resolution 48-51 on Friday evening, preserving Trump's authority for continued military operations. A Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Friday evening, with Qatar's foreign minister describing 'progress on a framework' for Hormuz negotiations, though Iranian officials offered no public confirmation. Iran's judiciary chief Gharibabadi declared the US naval blockade an 'act of war' under international law, as satellite imagery and shipping data revealed at least 14 Iranian tankers — including several previously sanctioned vessels — massing near Bandar Abbas and Jask in what analysts described as preparations to run the blockade. The IRGC escalated its regional campaign by striking a civilian oil storage facility in Sitra, Bahrain — the first confirmed attack on civilian infrastructure in a Gulf state — and claimed hits on US Patriot radar installations at Bahrain's al-Riffa and Awali air bases, though CENTCOM denied any damage to American systems. The IRGC also claimed to have downed a 58th MQ-9 Reaper drone and two additional MQ-1 Predator drones (the 19th and 20th claimed since the war began). Houthi forces were observed building tunnel networks and reinforced fortifications along the Bab al-Mandeb coastline, further consolidating their grip on the second critical maritime chokepoint alongside their ongoing operations near Hormuz approaches.

Financial markets endured a bruising end to the week before stabilizing Monday. Gold crashed to $3,532/oz — its fifth straight daily decline and a 10% weekly loss — hitting the lowest level since March 2025 as the strong US dollar, expectations of a December Fed rate hike (CME FedWatch odds above 90% for 25bp), and a sharp unwinding of the geopolitical risk premium crushed precious metals. The S&P 500 posted its worst weekly loss (-8.6%) since the Iran war began, while copper plunged 9.3% weekly on global demand fears. Oil bucked the broader rout: Brent crude rebounded to approximately $92.57/bbl on Monday morning futures, up from last week's $90.15 close, as weekend attack reports and Iran's blockade-breaking preparations offset the bearish macro backdrop. WTI rose to approximately $83.98/bbl. Despite the recovery, Brent has fallen nearly one-fifth from its November peak above $116. US gasoline dropped to $3.69/gal (AAA) — the lowest price since the Iran war began in February — providing rare consumer relief. Coal eased to approximately $139.50/tonne, extending its retreat from October highs. UKMTO's weekly transit report showed 263 ships crossing Hormuz during November 12-18, down 15% week-on-week, with oil tanker transits falling sharply from 52 to just 37 — a 29% decline — signaling growing shipper reluctance despite CENTCOM's escort operations. VLCC rates continued their descent, with the MEG-China TD3C spot rate softening further below $1M/day.

UKMTO reported two separate tanker attacks near Khasab, Oman on November 21 — both vessels suffered engine-room fires consistent with projectile strikes, with crews evacuated safely by Omani Coast Guard. On November 22, UKMTO issued an advisory about a tanker incident involving military forces near Charbahar in Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan province — details remained sparse, with the vessel's flag state requesting information. Saudi air defenses intercepted three ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh on Friday, following the interception of five drones and three ballistic missiles the previous day — the heaviest single-day salvo aimed at the capital since the war's early weeks. The Saudi-led coalition continued sustained operations against Houthi positions, with the coalition command reporting strikes on underground weapons storage facilities in Dhamar and launch platforms near Hodeidah. The IRGC's attack on the Sitra oil facility in Bahrain marked a significant escalation: unlike previous strikes that targeted military installations, the Sitra facility is a civilian petroleum processing and storage complex operated by BAPCO, Bahrain's national oil company. Bahrain's foreign ministry condemned the strike as 'an act of terrorism against civilian infrastructure' and reiterated its invocation of UN Charter Article 51. The broader pattern of declining Hormuz transits — with UKMTO data showing a 15% weekly decline in total ship crossings and a 29% drop in oil tanker transits — suggested that the cumulative effect of mine claims, projectile attacks, and elevated war-risk insurance ($64M per transit) was progressively deterring commercial shipping, even as CENTCOM maintained its escort corridor.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices eased from June-July peaks of $1,100-1,300/tonne to $740-890/tonne by mid-October (Kpler), but remain above pre-war avg of ~$500/tonne (CRU). ADNOC sees sulfur output doubling from 7M to 14-20M tonnes by 2030-2035 — CEO Al Jaberi calls sulfur 'the future gold' (Nov 18). ADNOC's Oct official selling price cut $70 to $890/tonne. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for sixth consecutive month — September through late November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warned 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urged US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). WHO: Yemen death toll since August escalation reaches 2,260, with 10,519 wounded; UNICEF: 330,000+ displaced including 174,000 children. Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Poland's Orlen becomes first buyer to terminate QatarEnergy LNG contract (1M tonnes/yr, oil-linked, through 2034) citing ongoing force majeure — observers warn more pullbacks possible (S&P Global Platts, Nov 11). DES NW Europe LNG benchmark at $27.59/MMBtu on Nov 11, up 175% YoY. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year. IMF projects 2026 GDP contractions: Kuwait and Iraq ~16%, Qatar ~15%. LNG flows at 40-45% of prewar levels.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B. Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030.
